audit.appendOnlyBody: The database refuses UPDATE and DELETE on this table through a trigger, so an event cannot be altered or removed after the fact — including by Velnox itself.
audit.subtitle: Every authentication and authorisation event, oldest kept, newest first.

clusters.addSubtitle: Three steps. The middle one is what makes the connection safe, and it cannot be skipped.
clusters.authKindHint: An API token is scoped, revocable on the Proxmox side, and survives a password change.
clusters.cephSubtitle: Health, daemons and the flags that are set.
clusters.confirmBody: Sign in to the node over SSH or the console and compare. This is the whole security of the connection: from here on, Velnox talks to that one certificate and refuses anything else.
clusters.confirmCheckbox: I have compared this fingerprint on the node and it matches.
clusters.confirmTitle: Check this fingerprint on the node itself
clusters.connectionSubtitle: How Velnox reaches this cluster, and what it checks before it speaks.
clusters.createExplainer: The credential is stored encrypted and then proved against the certificate you confirmed. If it does not work, nothing is added.
clusters.failingBody: Their inventory is whatever was last read successfully. Open one to see what the last run failed on.
clusters.failingTitle: Some clusters could not be read
clusters.fingerprintExplainer: Every connection is checked against this before anything is sent. A certificate that does not match closes the connection with the credential still unsent.
clusters.hostHint: A hostname or address of any node. Proxmox answers for the whole cluster from any of them.
clusters.name: Name
clusters.nooutBody: Ceph will not mark an OSD out while this flag is set, so a failed disk causes no rebalance and nothing turns red. It is usually left behind after maintenance. Clear it unless maintenance is in progress right now.
clusters.notProxmoxBody: Something answered, but not the way Proxmox does. Check the port, and check that you are not looking at a reverse proxy in front of it.
clusters.notProxmoxTitle: That does not look like a Proxmox API
clusters.pageDescription: Proxmox VE clusters and standalone nodes.
clusters.passwordWarning: A password gives Velnox everything that account can do, has to be renewed every two hours, and stops working when it is changed. An API token is better in all three respects.
clusters.probeExplainer: Velnox connects and reads the certificate. No token, no password and no cookie is sent — nobody has said yet that this is the right machine.
clusters.removeBody: The cluster itself is untouched and the audit trail stays. What is removed is what Velnox has cached about it, and the stored credential.
clusters.removeSectionBody: Nodes and guests go with it. A node cannot be removed on its own: it is in the inventory because the cluster reports it, and the next read would bring it back.
clusters.runsSubtitle: When Velnox last read this cluster, and anything it could not read.
clusters.siteHint: Optional. A site lets a permission cover one location rather than the whole customer.
clusters.staleWarning: Everything below is what was last read successfully, not what is true now.
clusters.step2: Step 2 — is this the right machine
clusters.subtitle: Proxmox VE clusters and standalone nodes under management, and when each was last read.
clusters.title: Clusters
clusters.tokenIdHint: As Proxmox shows it, including the realm and the token name.

library.full: The library would grow past its limit of {ceilingGb} GB: {usedGb} GB is in use and this needs {requestedGb} GB. Remove files, or raise VELNOX_LIBRARY_MAX_GB.
library.disk_low: That would leave {freeGb} GB of disk minus {requestedGb} GB, below the minimum of {floorGb} GB that must stay free. Free up space, or lower VELNOX_LIBRARY_MIN_FREE_GB.
library.invalid_filename: “{filename}” cannot be used as a filename. Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores — the characters Proxmox keeps.
library.unsupported_kind: “{filename}” is not an ISO (.iso) or a disk image Proxmox can import (.qcow2, .raw, .img).
library.duplicate_filename: The library already has a file called {filename}.
library.not_ready: That file is not ready yet.
library.in_use: A job is using this file right now. Wait for it to finish, or cancel it.
library.upload_offset: The upload is at byte {expected}, not {got}. Continue from there.
library.upload_too_large: That is more than the upload has room for.
library.url_refused: Velnox will not fetch from that address: only http and https, no credentials in the URL, and never loopback, link-local or Velnox’s own networks.
library.url_failed: The server did not hand the file over. Open the URL in a browser to see what it answers.
library.url_too_many_redirects: The URL redirected more than five times.
library.size_mismatch: The file did not arrive whole: the number of bytes is not the number promised.
library.wrong_content: {filename} is not what its name says. A file ending in .iso must be an ISO image; an error page saved under that name is the usual cause.
library.checksum_mismatch: Proxmox received {filename} with a different checksum from the library’s copy, and refused it.
library.storage_unsuitable: Storage {storage} on {node} does not take {content} content, or is not active.
library.storage_full: Storage {storage} has {freeGb} GB free; this needs {neededGb} GB.
library.already_on_storage: {volid} is already on that storage. Delete it there first to replace it.
library.file_missing: The file has gone from the library’s disk. Remove this entry and add the file again.
library.upload_abandoned: This upload was never finished, and was removed after a day.
library.resume_mismatch: That is not the file this upload started with. Choose the same file — same name, same size — to continue it.
library.upload_paused: The upload was paused. Choose the same file again to continue from where it stopped.

updates.afterwards: Five to ten minutes, most of it rebuilding images. Your .env is never regenerated, so secrets, the site address, the TLS mode and the ports all survive. Named volumes are untouched, so the database and the queue survive.
updates.backupBody: This is the step people skip, and it is the one that makes the other two reversible. An upgrade applies migrations, and a migration is not undone by checking out the previous commit.
updates.procedureBody: Three commands, in this order, from a shell on the host as a user with sudo.
updates.runningBody: Reported by the API, so it is the software actually serving this page.
updates.step1Hint: Writes a dated dump to /var/backups. Copy it somewhere that is not this machine.
updates.step2: 2. See what you are about to get
updates.step2Hint: Lists the commits between the running build and the upstream branch. Read them before pulling.
updates.step3Hint: The installer rebuilds the images, applies migrations, restarts the services and verifies the result.
updates.verifyBody: The same verification the installer runs at the end. Worth running again on its own after any change to the machine.

sso.cardDescription: Read from the directory at sign-in. Velnox stores no directory passwords.
sso.clientSecretHint: Stored encrypted. It is never shown again after saving.
sso.clientSecretStored: A secret is stored. Leave blank to keep it, or enter a new one to replace it.
sso.discoveryUrlHint: The OpenID configuration endpoint for your tenant. Must be HTTPS and publicly resolvable.
sso.notAvailableBody: This build can hold and check the configuration. Signing in through Entra ID arrives in a later phase, so the button is not shown on the sign-in page yet.
sso.subtitle: Sign in with a Microsoft Entra ID directory.
sso.testOk: The provider answered and the discovery document is valid.

identifiers.body: The Overview page of your new app registration shows both. Paste them here.
identifiers.clientHint: Also on the Overview page. Not the object ID.
identifiers.derived: Velnox will use this discovery document, built from the tenant ID:
identifiers.tenantHint: A GUID on the Overview page of the app registration.
identifiers.title: Copy the two identifiers back

intro.body: Connecting a directory means switching between this page and the Microsoft Entra admin center a few times. Here is what you will need.
intro.need1: Access to the Microsoft Entra admin center at entra.microsoft.com.
intro.need2: Permission to create an app registration — Application Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator or Global Administrator.
intro.need3: A few minutes without interruption: a client secret is shown only once, immediately after you create it.
intro.title: Before you start

register.accountTypes: For account types, choose "Accounts in this organizational directory only" unless you deliberately want guests from other tenants to sign in.
register.body: In the Entra admin center go to Identity → Applications → App registrations, and choose New registration. Use these two values.
register.redirectHint: Add it under platform "Web". It must match exactly — a trailing slash is a different URI to Entra.
register.title: Create the app registration

restrict.body: Optional. Limiting the email domains that may sign in is worth doing if your directory contains guest accounts.
restrict.title: Restrict who may sign in

secret.alreadyStored: A secret is already stored. Leave this blank to keep it, or paste a new one to replace it.
secret.body: In the app registration go to Certificates & secrets → Client secrets → New client secret. Copy the Value, not the Secret ID.
secret.hint: Entra shows the value once. If you navigate away before copying it, delete the secret and create another.
secret.title: Create a client secret

test.body: Velnox will store the configuration and ask the provider for its discovery document, so you find out now rather than at the first sign-in.
test.secretEntered: A new secret will be stored
test.secretMissing: None — the connection will not work without one
test.title: Save and check the connection

system.migrationsUnknown: Database is ahead of this build: {names}
system.subtitle: Live readiness of this installation
system.title: Service status
system.workerHint: The worker has no network port by design; its liveness is reported through a heartbeat.

tenants.archiveExplanation: Nothing is deleted. The tenant stops appearing in lists and its audit trail stays readable. Every account in it has to be disabled first.
tenants.mspCannotBeArchived: The MSP organisation cannot be suspended or archived. Doing so would disable the accounts that administer this installation, including yours.
tenants.name: Name
tenants.ownCannotBeArchived: You cannot archive the tenant your own account belongs to.
tenants.pageDescription: Customer organisations, and the MSP organisation itself.
tenants.slugDerived: The short identifier used in URLs is derived from the name.
tenants.subtitle: The MSP organisation and the customers it manages. Isolation between them is enforced in the data layer, not by this list.
tenants.title: Tenants
tenants.parentHint: Roles held in the main tenant apply in its sub-tenants. This cannot be changed later.
tenants.noMains: There is no main tenant yet to create a sub-tenant under.

tls.changeBody: The way back when this page cannot be reached — after a certificate browsers refuse, for instance. Run one of these on the host as a user with sudo; it hands the choice back to the installer’s.
tls.commandSelfSigned: Go back to a self-signed certificate
tls.commandUpload: Install a certificate you already have
tls.configuredBody: What this installation is set up to serve.
tls.daysRemaining: {days, plural, =0 {last day} one {# day left} other {# days left}}
tls.expiredBody: Browsers are refusing this installation. Install a new certificate or switch mode with one of the commands below.
tls.expiringAcme: Caddy renews automatically, usually 30 days before expiry. If this warning does not clear, check that the address still resolves publicly and ports 80 and 443 are reachable.
tls.expiringManual: This certificate was supplied by you, so nothing renews it automatically. Install the replacement before it expires.
tls.expiringTitle: {days, plural, one {The certificate expires in # day} other {The certificate expires in # days}}
tls.mismatchBody: None of the names on this certificate cover {address}. Browsers will refuse the connection rather than warn about it.
tls.mismatchTitle: This certificate does not cover the address

modeExplained.acme: Caddy obtains and renews a publicly trusted certificate over ACME. It needs the address to resolve publicly and ports 80 and 443 to reach this host.
modeExplained.certificate: A certificate you supplied is being served. Nothing renews it automatically; replace it before it expires.
modeExplained.internal: A certificate from Caddy's own certificate authority. Browsers warn once, because they have never heard of that authority. Right for an appliance reached by IP address on a management network.

tls.noCertificateBody: The proxy answered but presented no certificate. That normally means it is still starting, or an ACME order has not completed yet.
tls.servedBody: Read by opening a real TLS connection to the proxy a moment ago — not from configuration. If this disagrees with the configuration above, a change was written and never picked up.
tls.subject: Issued to
tls.subtitle: The certificate this installation serves, and how to change it.
tls.unreachableBody: No TLS handshake with the proxy ({detail}). Velnox itself is running — you are reading this — so the proxy is probably restarting.
tls.whyNotHere: scripts/tls.sh writes the installer’s certificate files and restarts the proxy. A certificate chosen above is handed back to it when the script runs.
tls.changeInterfaceBody: Applied through the proxy’s admin socket. A configuration the proxy cannot serve is refused, and the current certificate stays in place. The certificate served afterwards is read back to check it.

choiceHint.installer: What the installer set up, from VELNOX_TLS, and what scripts/tls.sh changes.
choiceHint.internal: Browsers warn once. Right for an appliance reached by IP address on a management network.
choiceHint.acme: Publicly trusted. The address must resolve publicly and ports 80 and 443 must reach this host. Another ACME authority can be named instead.
choiceHint.certificate: Upload a certificate with its chain and its private key. Nothing renews it: replace it before it expires.

tls.acmeNeedsHostname: Not for an IP address: Let’s Encrypt issues for host names only.
tls.acmeEmailHint: Where the ACME authority writes about expiring certificates and problems.
tls.otherAcme: Use another ACME authority (a private CA, or a staging server)
tls.acmeDirectoryHint: The authority’s directory URL, https only.
tls.acmeRootHint: PEM. Needed when the authority’s own HTTPS is not signed by a publicly trusted root.
tls.certificateFieldHint: The certificate first, then the intermediates — your provider’s fullchain file.
tls.keyFieldHint: Stored encrypted. It is never shown again, and never leaves the installation through this page.
tls.breakGlass: If a certificate makes this page unreachable, run sudo bash /opt/velnox/scripts/tls.sh --self-signed on the host: it hands the choice back to the installer’s.
tls.appliedVerifiedBody: The certificate the proxy serves now is the one chosen.
tls.appliedAcmePending: The proxy is obtaining the certificate; that can take a minute. Open this page again shortly.
tls.appliedNotVerifiedBody: The proxy accepted the configuration, but still serves another certificate. Open this page again in a moment.

warning.not_covering: The certificate does not cover this installation’s address. Browsers will refuse it until the address or the certificate changes.
warning.no_chain: Only one certificate was uploaded. Most browsers also need the issuer’s chain; upload the fullchain file.

users.createBody: Velnox sends no email, so there is no invitation. Set an initial password and pass it on yourself; the new account can change it after signing in.
users.disabledNotice: This account is disabled. Its sessions were revoked and it cannot sign in.
users.foundingBody: This is the account the setup wizard created, and the way back into a misconfigured installation. Its roles cannot be taken away by anyone, including itself. Another administrator can disable it — but not while no other enabled account can administer this installation.
users.initialPasswordHint: At least {min} characters, held to the same rule as every other password.
users.managementPendingBody: Inviting users, assigning roles and deactivating accounts arrive with the roles interface. The accounts above are read from the API.
users.mfaGapTitle: {count, plural, one {# privileged account without a second factor} other {# privileged accounts without a second factor}}
users.noRoles: No roles — this account can sign in but do nothing.
users.resetMfaBlockedMsp: This account is in the MSP organisation, and can reach every customer. Removing its second factor requires an MSP Super Administrator.
users.resetMfaBlockedSelf: You cannot remove your own second factor here. Use Security, which asks for a code from your authenticator — that request is what proves you still hold it.
users.subtitle: Accounts that can sign in to this installation.

library.subtitle: ISOs and cloud images on the Velnox host, ready to copy onto any cluster.
library.capacityDescription: How much the library can hold. It may use up to {maxGb} GB, and always leaves {minFreeGb} GB free on the disk for the database.
library.capacityUsed: {used} of {ceiling} used. There is room for {room} more.
library.addDescription: From a URL, which the worker fetches, or from this browser, sent in pieces that survive a dropped connection.
library.fromUrlHint: http or https. The address is shown and logged without its query string, which is where download links keep their token.
library.fromUploadHint: .iso for installers; .img, .qcow2 or .raw for cloud images.
library.itemsDescription: Each file under its friendly name, with the name Proxmox will give it underneath.
library.name: Name
library.pushNoStorage: No active storage on this cluster takes {content} content.
library.pushExplain: Proxmox checks the file against its checksum as it arrives. If the copy is cancelled or fails, nothing is left on the node.
library.renameDescription: The file keeps its name {filename}; this changes only how Velnox shows it.
library.renameNameHint: Read from the filename as: {parsed}. Leave empty to keep that.
library.renameKeepLanguage: Keep the language read from the filename ({language})
library.renameLanguageHint: A language code such as nl, en-GB or de. Leave empty for none.
library.removeBody: The file is deleted from the library. Copies already on clusters are left alone.
library.capacityDiskLimits: The disk is what limits it: {free} is free there, and {floor} of that has to stay free.
library.uploadBackground: You can go to other pages while this runs; it is shown at the bottom of the window. Reloading or closing the page stops it — it can be resumed from here with the same file.

autoconfig.subtitle: Templates that VMs are built from: Windows with an answer file, Linux from a cloud image.
autoconfig.name: Name
autoconfig.ownerHint: An MSP template can be offered to every customer or to chosen ones; a customer’s own is theirs only.
autoconfig.visibilityHint: Every customer may build from it, only the customers chosen below, or only its owner.
autoconfig.missingSecrets: This template cannot build a VM until these are set: {keys}.
autoconfig.cloneDescription: The copy is independent of the original. Settings are copied; stored passwords and keys are not, and have to be set again.
autoconfig.removeBody: The template and its stored secrets are deleted. VMs built from it keep their records.
autoconfig.readOnly: You can see these templates and build from them; changing them needs autoconfig.manage.
autoconfig.notYours: This template belongs to someone else. You can build from it or clone it, not change it.
autoconfig.deliveryVelnoxHint: The mail links to the VM; revealing its passwords in Velnox is recorded.
autoconfig.deliveryPdfHint: The mail carries an AES-256 PDF with the passwords. Its password is never in the same mail.
autoconfig.pdfShownOnce: Shown once to whoever asks for the VM
autoconfig.chooseFile: Choose a file from the library
autoconfig.editionFromIso: The editions read from this ISO. Setup installs the one with exactly this name.
autoconfig.editionTyped: The edition list could not be read from this ISO, so the name is typed and not checked. It must match the ISO exactly.
autoconfig.diskLayoutHint: GPT is recommended: UEFI, Secure Boot, a TPM, disks past 2 TB. Windows 11 needs it.
autoconfig.productKeyHint: Five groups of five, separated by dashes. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
autoconfig.noKeyHint: Without a key, Setup does not stop for one; Windows asks at activation when the edition needs one.
autoconfig.regionHint: Four separate settings, so a Dutch installation can type on US-International.
autoconfig.ianaHint: An IANA zone, such as Europe/Amsterdam.
autoconfig.windowsAccountsHint: The built-in Administrator is always given a password; on a desktop edition it is switched off after the first logon, so name at least one administrator here.
autoconfig.linuxAccountsHint: Sudo users with a key are the default. Root login stays off unless you turn it on.
autoconfig.passwordRule: At least twelve characters, with three of: upper case, lower case, digits, symbols. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
autoconfig.rdp: Remote Desktop, with its firewall rule
autoconfig.updateDuringSetup: During Setup — can take an hour
autoconfig.mirrorHint: The recommendation is a CDN or a geo-selecting list, never a single fixed server.
autoconfig.sshKeysHint: One per line, as in authorized_keys.
autoconfig.sshEnabled: SSH server, with the keys placed
autoconfig.sshPasswords: Allow SSH logins with a password
autoconfig.packagesHint: Debian package names, separated by spaces.
autoconfig.cpuTypeHint: host is faster, and stops live migration between different CPUs.
autoconfig.visibilitySelectedCount: {count, plural, one {# chosen customer} other {# chosen customers}}
autoconfig.offeredToHint: Only these customers see it and may build from it. They do not see who else is offered it. MSP staff can always use it.
autoconfig.perTenantHint: A customer left empty gets a password generated for each VM. Only the MSP sets these, and customers never see them.
autoconfig.installerPackagesHint: MSIs and EXEs of this template’s owner, run in this order after Windows is installed, from a CD of their own. Velnox reads how each one ended and shows it in the build’s job.
autoconfig.packagesNeedAgent: Packages need the QEMU guest agent: it is how Velnox learns how they ended. Switch it on under Installer.
autoconfig.packagesNone: No packages: nothing extra is installed.
autoconfig.packageGone: This package no longer exists. Remove it from the template.
autoconfig.packageHidden: A package of the template’s owner
autoconfig.packageArgumentsHint: Put on the installer’s command line as written. For an MSI, /qn /norestart installs quietly without restarting; %ProgramFiles% and quotes work.
autoconfig.packageRequired: Required: if it fails, the build fails and the VM is removed
autoconfig.noPackages: No ready packages for this owner
autoconfig.packagesSubtitle: MSIs and EXEs per tenant, for Windows templates to run after installation. A tenant’s packages are visible to that tenant only.
autoconfig.packagesTenantHint: Packages belong to one tenant. Choose whose packages to see or add.
autoconfig.packagesListHint: Uploads continue in the background, shown in the activity bar. A package can be used once it is Ready.
autoconfig.packagesEmpty: This tenant has no packages yet.
autoconfig.removePackageBody: {filename} is removed from Velnox. VMs that already installed it keep it.

provisioning.subtitle: Every VM built from an Autoconfig template, with its installation record. VMs still being built also show under Virtual Machines.
provisioning.empty: No VMs have been built from templates yet.
provisioning.newDescription: From a template, onto a cluster. The installation runs by itself.
provisioning.noTemplates: No complete template is offered to this cluster’s tenant.
provisioning.hostnameHint: Without a domain, at most {max} characters.

hostnameProblem.characters: Letters, digits and dashes only, not starting or ending with a dash.
hostnameProblem.digits_only: A hostname cannot be only digits.

provisioning.mediaHintWindows: Takes ISO content. The installer is copied there from the library if it is missing.
provisioning.mediaHintLinux: Takes ISO and import content. The cloud image is copied there from the library if it is missing.
provisioning.notify: Mail me when it is ready
provisioning.queuedBody: Follow the job to watch it, or open the record. You can leave this page.
provisioning.documentPasswordTitle: The password of the installation record
provisioning.documentPasswordBody: The record mailed to you is encrypted with this password. It is shown now and never again, and it is not in the mail. Keep it somewhere safe.
provisioning.credentialsDescription: Showing them is recorded in the audit log, and they disappear from this page after five minutes.
provisioning.credentialsGone: The passwords of this VM are no longer kept in Velnox.

mail.subtitle: How Velnox sends mail: when a VM is ready, and later for other notifications.
mail.verifiedAt: A test went out with these settings on {when}.
mail.serverDescription: Changing any of this switches mail off until a new test goes out.
mail.securityNoneHint: Only for a relay on the same host or in a lab: anything sent can be read on the way.
mail.passwordStored: A password is stored. Type a new one to replace it.
mail.saved: Saved. Send a test before switching mail on.
mail.testDescription: The worker sends the test with the stored settings, as it will send every mail.

activity.title: Running jobs
activity.running: {count, plural, =0 {none running} one {# running} other {# running}}
activity.jobsTitle: Jobs, and those finished in the last half hour
activity.recent: Finished in the last half hour
activity.empty: No jobs running, and none finished in the last half hour.

support.title: Support logs
support.description: For a support case: what Velnox did for the tenants in view — jobs with their steps and output, discovery runs — and the Proxmox tasks of their nodes, each marked with whether Velnox or someone outside Velnox started it.
support.exportHint: JSON Lines, for the tenant and period chosen above; without a period, as far back as Proxmox tasks are kept. The download is recorded in the audit log.
support.retentionReadOnly: Proxmox tasks are kept for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.

nodeUpdates.subtitle: What each node would update, updating one, and the policies and windows that decide when.
nodeUpdates.nodesBody: Read with every discovery. Security updates, kernels and Proxmox’s own packages are counted apart; a reboot is due when a newer kernel is installed than the one running.
nodeUpdates.needsSsh: Needs SSH on the cluster, with this node’s key confirmed.
nodeUpdates.runBody: Runs apt-get dist-upgrade on the node over SSH, as a job you can follow line by line. It cannot be undone, and a cancel waits for it to finish.
nodeUpdates.rebootHint: A reboot shuts down the guests running on the node unless they are moved first; it is only done when the cluster keeps quorum without the node.
nodeUpdates.policyApplies: The cluster’s policy “{policy}” applies: its approval and maintenance window too.
nodeUpdates.policyBody: One policy per cluster. Saving one for a cluster replaces the policy it had.
nodeUpdates.windowHint: Updates under this policy run only while this window is open — started by hand or by the policy.
nodeUpdates.enabledHint: A disabled policy applies to nothing.
nodeUpdates.requireApprovalHint: Every update under this policy waits for someone with updates.execute to approve it.
nodeUpdates.autoApplyHint: When the window opens, Velnox updates the cluster’s nodes that have pending updates, one at a time. Needs a window.
nodeUpdates.policiesBody: How each cluster is updated. A cluster without a policy is updated by hand only, at any time.
nodeUpdates.windowBody: When the window opens, in its own time zone, and how long it stays open. It opens at the same local time on the days the clocks change.
nodeUpdates.monthDayHint: A number (1, 15, -1 for the last day) or a weekday with its place: 1SA is the first Saturday, -1SU the last Sunday.
nodeUpdates.rruleHint: An RFC 5545 rule: FREQ (DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY) with BYDAY, BYMONTHDAY, BYHOUR and BYMINUTE. Other parts are refused rather than guessed.
nodeUpdates.blackoutHint: Local dates as YYYY-MM-DD, separated by commas.
nodeUpdates.neverOpens: Does not open in the coming year
nodeUpdates.windowsBody: Windows belong to a tenant and are used by that tenant’s policies.
nodeUpdates.historyBody: Every node update, by a person or by a policy. Open one for its output.
nodeUpdates.rollingBody: Each node in turn: its running guests moved to the others, updated, rebooted if needed, checked, and the guests moved back. The cluster never loses quorum, and the run does not start on a cluster that is already degraded.
nodeUpdates.capacityShort: While {node} is down, its guests need {needed} GB and the other nodes have {free} GB free.
nodeUpdates.concurrencyHint: At most {max} on this cluster without losing quorum.
nodeUpdates.nonMigratable: A guest that cannot move live
nodeUpdates.nonMigratableHint: A guest with a disk on a node’s own storage, or a device passed through, cannot move to another node while running.

nonMigratablePolicy.SHUTDOWN: Shut it down for its node’s reboot, start it after

nodeUpdates.settleHint: How long a node, the cluster and Ceph may take to be whole again after a reboot before the run stops.
nodeUpdates.migrateBackHint: Each guest returns to the node it came from once that node is done.

placement.subtitle: Which guests of a cluster are kept apart or together, which nodes a guest belongs on, and whether that holds now.
placement.chooseClusterBody: Choose a cluster to see its placement rules.
placement.haRulesOn: Every node runs Proxmox VE 9: each rule is also one of Proxmox’s own HA rules, so it holds while Velnox is not running.
placement.haRulesOff: Proxmox VE 8 has no rules of its own for this: Velnox keeps them, by moving guests.
placement.notWhole: The cluster is not whole — a node is offline or quorum is lost. Placement moves nothing until it is.
placement.rulesBody: Whether a rule holds is read from the inventory. Only running guests count: a stopped guest is nowhere.

kindHint.KEEP_APART: These guests never run on the same node — for the two halves of a cluster, or a primary and its replica.
kindHint.KEEP_TOGETHER: These guests always run on the same node — for guests that talk to each other constantly.
kindHint.PREFER_NODES: These guests run on the nodes chosen — for licensing, hardware or a quiet node.

placement.preferSoft: {guests} run on {nodes} when one of them can.
placement.name: Name
placement.strictHint: Off, a guest may run elsewhere when none of these nodes can take it.
placement.nowBody: Correcting moves running guests live until every rule holds, without breaking another. Balancing moves one guest, within the rules, when memory use differs by more than the threshold below.
placement.settingsBody: Both off until you turn them on. Never while the cluster is not whole, never while another job changes it, and at most once per quiet period.
placement.autoCorrectHint: When a rule is not met, Velnox moves guests to meet it.
placement.balanceHint: When the busiest node uses more of its memory than the quietest by more than the threshold, Velnox moves one guest.
placement.quietHint: At least this long between two runs Velnox starts by itself.
placement.noJobs: Nothing has been moved for placement yet.

upgrades.noPlaybooks: No upgrade playbooks yet: the Ceph and Proxmox VE upgrades arrive in Phases 9A and 9B. Plans made earlier are listed below.
upgrades.plansBody: Each plan runs one playbook — checks, remediations, the upgrade target by target, validation — or, as a composite, several plans one after another.
upgrades.newBody: Targets come from the inventory: nodes by name, Ceph daemons in Ceph’s own order — monitors, managers, OSDs, then the rest.
upgrades.name: Name
upgrades.selftestComposite: As a composite: the daemon self-test, then the node self-test
upgrades.selftestApproval: With a change that needs approval
upgrades.cephTargetHint: From the version matrix: the release that runs now must be the one each step starts from.
upgrades.cephMdsHint: Only with CephFS: max_mds is 1 and standby replay is off for every file system, as Proxmox’s guide asks. Velnox restarts the MDS daemons one at a time and does not change those settings.
upgrades.pveCephFirstHint: Proxmox VE 9 needs Ceph Squid. Ticked, the plan is a composite: the Ceph upgrade, then — only if it completed — Proxmox VE, node by node.
